GZero 1.4 adds the analysis methods of our dithienylethene paper (Rashid et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 147, 830 (2025)), a tab for flickering and mechanical events, a tab for large-area (EGaIn) junctions, and, from v1.3, junction statistics and single-level / transition-voltage analysis of I-V curves.

**Windows download:** `GZero-v1.4-windows-x64.zip` below. Unzip it anywhere and double-click `GZero\GZero.exe`. You don't need Python. Keep the whole folder together; the exe doesn't work on its own. The user manual is in `GZero\docs\User_Manual.pdf`, and Help -> User manual (F1) opens it from inside the program. `selftest_report.txt` is the self-test of exactly this build.

Windows may show a SmartScreen warning because the exe isn't signed: click "More info", then "Run anyway".

Changes since v1.2:
- **Junction statistics** (new tab, manual 6.4): per-trace plateau detection with a slope test, junction yield (Kamenetska et al. 2009), plateau conductance per trace, and yield and conductance against trace number to see drift.
- **I-V** (manual 10.2-10.4): single-level model fit of every curve, of the mean curves and of the most probable curve; zero or finite temperature, either closed form or the energy-grid Landauer integral of Rashid et al. 2025; Levenberg-Marquardt or bounded fits; preset "Rashid et al. 2025". Transition voltage spectroscopy with eps0 and the bias asymmetry from both polarities (Beebe 2006, Baldea 2012).
- **Events** (new tab, manual 9.8): flickering and mechanical events in G(t) as in Rashid et al. 2025 (Butterworth + Savitzky-Golay + derivative peaks), and the conductance-time histogram of the holds with the most probable conductance.
- **EGaIn (ensemble)** (new tab, manual 10.5): one file per junction; shorts and yield, Gaussian log|J| per bias with junction-based confidence intervals (Reus et al. 2012), rectification, V_trans, single-level fit, and beta and J0 from a length series.
- **Flicker noise:** preset "Rashid et al. 2025" (Pearson r scan) and an *end points* setting.
- **Histograms:** dwell time of every fitted peak.
- The mean I-V curve leaves out the half sweeps at the start and end of a recording.

To run from source on any OS, see the README.
